memos.scout:
The strongest honest case is thin, and I'd lean toward skipping.

What the brief shows: the coin is alive at 30 minutes, has 306 buyers and 153 sellers over the last 15 minutes, $51k volume, and a 2.46x return over 30 minutes. Only a 4.3% drawdown from the 30-minute high, and net flow was positive (+20 SOL) in the last 15 minutes. Those are real signs of recent demand.

The case against is stronger. The first two minutes after graduation show 100% of early buying bundled, the top 3 curve buyers hold all the curve share, the top 5 buyers took 97% of early buys, and a launch bot was present. That is the factory pattern, which has lost about 46% per trade. Sell pressure is also building: 199 SOL sold against 220 bought in the last 15 minutes, with 153 sellers, so the recent net flow is buyer-driven only on paper. A 2.8x completer share on the curve fits concentrated accumulation rather than broad demand.

Against a $20 ticket and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, the thesis would need the 306 buyers to keep appearing after the bundled holders start distributing. Nothing in the brief shows that. I'd skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a rug or insider distribution by the bundled early wallets. The curve shows bundle_share 1.0, top3_share 1.0, and a launch bot present, so the supply is concentrated in coordinated wallets, not a broad crowd. The first 2 minutes after graduation show top5_buyer_share 0.967 and sell_to_buy_ratio 0.0176, meaning almost nothing sold early, which is typical of insiders holding for a later exit. The 30-minute return of +246% and the 226% 15-minute return are the kind of pump that tends to end with those holders selling into new buyers. The 15-minute net flow of only 20.2 SOL against 219.7 SOL bought and 199.5 SOL sold shows heavy churn: fees of 1.4-5.1% per round trip will eat any small move, and the pool depth of 161 SOL is thin for a $20 ticket. Skip.
